content: Bubbletea message ordering and goroutine pitfalls: (1) Commands run concurrently — messages arrive in non-deterministic order; never assume sequencing. (2) Use tea.Sequence() when strict ordering matters. (3) Raw goroutines that directly mutate model fields cause data races detectable by go -race. (4) Goroutine leaks: a tea.Cmd waiting on a channel forever keeps the program alive after tea.Quit — always provide cancellation. (5) Multiple bubbletea programs in succession (e.g., difftool mode launching one per file) accumulate signal handlers — use tea.WithoutSignalHandler and manage signals manually. (6) Framework-level race condition on repaint during resize exists in older versions (PR #330).
